repairs.value: Licona argues that Carrier’s coordinated-hallucination and legendary-gospel accounts strain the evidence, while earlier testimony and religious context make resurrection the uniquely plausible explanation of the data.

Strongest feature: Licona joins his coordination objection, pre-Markan chronology point, and religious-context appeal into a clear cumulative case that resurrection explains the agreed evidence without Carrier’s alleged strain. Principal limitation: His inference treats Carrier’s earlier account as matching, simultaneous multimodal hallucinations, although Carrier had described differing experiences converging through suggestion and memory contamination; because no later argumentative reply follows this closing, that prior qualification remains controlling. Live burden: Evaluators must decide whether early testimony establishes more than sincere belief, whether later legend can alter interpretation without creating that testimony, and whether religious context independently raises resurrection’s probability. Locked score: The fixed score of 75 rewards a focused synthesis and pertinent chronology defense, but reflects that his hallucination rebuttal targets a narrower mechanism than Carrier defended.

contextualSupport.reason: Carrier earlier distinguishes individual experiences while invoking suggestion, memory contamination, and separate circumstances for Paul.
Licona’s closing supplies the challenged characterization and concludes the formal rounds without a later argumentative response.
